## Project Overview

For this project, I selected three wide-format datasets to practice cleaning, transforming, and analyzing data using R. I will use `tidyr` and `dplyr` to convert the datasets into tidy long formats, then explore patterns and trends through summary tables and visualizations.

## Dataset 1: U.S. vs. China Military Expenditure (SIPRI)

I will use military expenditure data from SIPRI to compare spending trends between the United States and China. Since the dataset contains years as separate columns, I will use `pivot_longer()` to reorganize the data, clean missing values, and examine how military spending and the gap between the two countries have changed over time.

## Dataset 2: U.S. vs. China GDP (World Bank)

I will analyze World Bank GDP data to compare economic growth between the United States and China. I will transform the yearly GDP columns into a long format using `pivot_longer()`, calculate annual growth rates, and examine how the economic gap between the two countries has evolved.

## Dataset 3: National Park Water Chemistry (NPS)

I will use water quality monitoring data from the National Park Service, originally shared in Week 5 Discussion 5A. I will transform the wide-format chemistry measurements into a tidy long format, address missing values, and analyze how pH, nitrogen, and phosphorus measurements vary over time and across different monitoring sites.

## Tools and Methods

All three datasets will be imported into RStudio and processed using `tidyr` and `dplyr`. I will document each transformation, create summary tables and visualizations using `ggplot2`, and explain my findings in Quarto.
